newsitem.title: INDIA: Paribas lowers India M&M, TELCO.
newsitem.headline: Paribas lowers India M&M, TELCO.

text.p: Securities firm Paribas said on Thursday it was lowering its recommendations on leading Indian automobile firms Mahindra & Mahindra and TELCO to "hold" after a sharp rise in the stock prices of both firms.
"Both downgrades reflect the sharp rises in their stock prices recently, and not any changes in their fundamental outlook," analyst Rajeev Das said in a note to investors.
"The sharp jump in their stock prices has created an opportunity for investors to take profit."
Das said he was also lowering recommendations for the firms' global depositary receipts (GDRs) to a "sell" from "hold."

He said TELCO's shares looked ready to cross Paribas' price relative target of 440 rupees as well as their 52-week high of 439 rupees. TELCO shares ended 6.50 rupees lower at 434 on the Bombay bourse on Thursday.
"Since our last note on the company in late May, the shares have risen more than 11 percent while the market is up a little under 10 percent," Das said.
"With the stock reaching our price target, we are downgrading our recommendation from buy to no action even though the shares are still at a discount to the sector," he added.
Das said TELCO's GDR were trading at around a 25 premium to the local shares -- their highest premium in almost a year.
"With limited potential for the GDR to outperform the market further, we are downgrading our recommendation on the GDR to sell," he said.
Das said shares of tractor and utility vehicles maker Mahindra & Mahindra had staged a smart rally over the last week, driving past Paribas' price target of 402 rupees for the stock.
Shares of Mahindra -- which have risen 17 percent since the firm announced its 1996/97 (April-March) results on June 10 -- closed 5.0 rupees lower at 418.
"We think this outperformance precludes more gains on the shares; as such we are downgrading them to no action. Overall, the local shares look fairly valued by any valuation parameter," Das said.

He said many investors were turning away from the automobiles sector as the sector entered a phase of leaner growth. Mahindra, protected by strong demand in rural and semi-rural areas, was immune to this trend.
"Despite our favourable view on Mahindra's growth prospects, we are downgrading the local shares to no action, based purely on its current valuation," Das said.
"While there may be some more upside left, it would be hard for the stock to outperform the market over the next few months."
